For the year ended December 31, 2025, the total change in unrealized gains on physical silver bullion amounted to $8,520.5 million and there were no realized gains or losses, compared to the change in unrealized gains of $850.6 million and net realized losses of $1.4 million during the same period in 2024.
During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Trust issued 94,446,249 units through the at-the-market offering program (the “ATM Program”) for gross proceeds of $1,409.2 million, and redeemed 5,495 units for $0.1 million of cash. Comparatively, for the same period in 2024, the Trust issued 34,903,967 units for gross proceeds of $358.8 million, and redeemed 2,521,650 units for $20.5 million of silver bullion (including a partial cash outlay of $0.4 million) and 9,910 units for $0.1 million of cash.
The value of the net assets 1 of the Trust as at December 31, 2025 was $15,108.9 million or $24.59 per unit, compared to $5,227.4 million or $10.05 per unit as at December 31, 2024. The Trust held 210,706,099 troy ounce s of physical silver bullion as at December 31, 2025 compared to 180,613,426 troy ounce s as at December 31, 2024. As at December 31, 2025, the spot price of silver bullion was $71.66 per troy ounce compared to a spot price of silver bullion of $28.90 per troy ounce as at December 31, 2024. The Trust returned 144.6% compared to the return on spot silver of 148.0% for the year ended December 31, 2025. Comparatively, for the same period in 2024, the Trust returned 20.5% compared to the return on spot silver of 21.5%.
The units closed at $23.65 on the NYSE Arca and $23.66 on the TSX on December 31, 2025 compared to closing prices of $9.65 on the NYSE Arca and $9.65 on the TSX on December 31, 2024. These units are denominated in U.S. dollars on both exchanges. During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Trust’s units traded on the NYSE Arca at an average discount to net asset value of approximately 2.8%, compared to approximately 3.5% for the same period in 2024.
The Trust pays its own expenses, which include, but are not limited to, audit, legal and trustee fees, unitholder reporting expenses, general and administrative fees, filing and listing fees payable to applicable securities regulatory authorities and stock exchanges, storage fees for the physical silver bullion, and any expenses associated with the implementation and ongoing operation of the Independent Review Committee of the Trust. Operating expenses 1 for the year ended December 31 , 2025 amounted to $5.9 million compared to $4.8 million for the same period in 2024. Operating expenses for the year ended December 31, 2025 amounted to 0.08% of the average net assets 2 during the period on an annualized basis, compared to 0.10% for the same period in 2024.
The Trust pays the Manager, a monthly management fee equal to 1⁄12 of 0.45% of the value of the net assets of the Trust (determined in accordance with the Trust’s trust agreement), plus any applicable sales taxes. The management fee is calculated and accrued daily and payable monthly in arrears on the last day of each month. For the year ended December 31 , 2025, the Trust incurred management fees of $35.1 million compared to $22.3 million for the same period in 2024. As at December 31, 2025, the Trust has no management fee payable 3 compared to $2.2 million as at December 31, 2024.
1 The operating expenses non-GAAP measure is calculated for the year ended December 31, 2025 as total expenses per the statements of comprehensive income (loss) less management fees of $35.1 million, sales tax of $2.7 million, and net foreign exchange losses (gains) of $nil (amounts for the year ended December 31, 2024 were $22.3 million, $1.6 million and $nil, respectively).

The investment objective of the Trust is to provide a secure, convenient and exchange-traded investment alternative for investors interested in holding physical silver bullion without the inconvenience that is typical of a direct investment in physical silver bullion. The Trust invests and intends to continue to invest primarily in long-term holdings of unencumbered, fully allocated, physical silver bullion and does not speculate with regard to short-term changes in silver prices. The Trust will only purchase and expects only to own “Good Delivery Bars” as defined by the London Bullion Market Association (“LBMA”), with each bar purchased being verified against the LBMA source by representatives from the Trust’s custodian, the Royal Canadian Mint.
Significant risks that are relevant to the Trust are discussed here. General information on risks and risk management is described in Note 6 of the Generic Notes.
If the market value of silver bullion increased by 1 %, with all other variables held constant, this would have increased total equity and comprehensive income by approximately $ 151.0 million (December 31, 2024: $ 52.2 million); conversely, if the value of silver bullion decreased by 1 %, this would have decreased total equity and comprehensive income by the same amount.
As at December 31, 2025, approximately ($ 792 ) (December 31, 2024: ($ 253 ) ) of the Trust’s other assets and accounts payable were denominated in Canadian dollars. As a result, a 1 % change in the exchange rate between the Canadian and U.S. dollars would not have a material impact to the Trust.
The Trust’s risk is concentrated in physical silver bullion held across two locations, whose value constitutes 58.2 % and 41.7 % of total equity as at December 31, 2025 ( 59.6 %, 32.0 %, and 8.3 % of total equity held across three locations as at December 31, 2024).
